patch.description:
Has a helper on the checkpoint's cluster delete its files (chosen as for the files
endpoints: any helper for a remote checkpoint, the node holding it for a local one),
then marks the checkpoint deprecated. A checkpoint without a path has no files to
delete and is just deprecated. One with files but no cluster to ask (not taken
through a checkpoint action) is kept, with a 409, rather than deprecated with its
files left behind. If the helper fails to delete, the checkpoint is left as it was
and the helper's error is returned. Concurrent requests for the same checkpoint may
both ask for the delete; whichever marks it deprecated first wins, the other gets 404.
